cleanIntro: The Oculus22 is a rimfire can, which means it is designed to come apart often — .22 LR is dirty, unjacketed and waxy, and the baffles will lead up faster than any centrefire can you own. It is built as a main body holding five baffles plus a screw-on ADAPT Module holding five more, and the whole job is done with the provided disassembly tool, a hex key and a wooden dowel. Rugged's own limits shape everything below: no vise and no pliers, no disassembly while the can is on the gun, and a re-check of the thread between magazines rather than at some round count. The Oculus22 is a suppressor and not a firearm — clearing the host is the host's own manual's job.

steps.title: Clear the host, then take the Oculus22 off it before anything else
steps.action: Magazine out, action open, chamber checked by eye and by finger — and then the can comes off the gun before a single part of it is touched. Rugged states this twice in one paragraph, and the second half is the one people skip: the Oculus22 is not disassembled while it is attached to the host firearm. That means the first operation of a teardown is unscrewing the whole can from the muzzle, not unscrewing the front cap. How your rifle or pistol clears is a question for its own operator's manual, which this book does not attempt to answer.
steps.prose: Rimfire hosts are the ones most likely to be semi-autos that do not lock back, so the chamber check is a real check and not a formality.
steps.quote: WARNING! Before disassembling your Oculus22™, first remove the magazine and check the chamber of the firearm to confirm that it is in a safe condition and completely unloaded. Do not disassemble your Oculus22 while the suppressor is attached to the host firearm. Remove the suppressor before disassembly. Failure to do so could result in serious personal injury or death.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Oculus Disassembly, p.1
steps.warn: Remove the Oculus22 from the host firearm BEFORE disassembly, every time.

steps.title: No vise, no pliers, no improvised tools on the Oculus22
steps.action: Get the provided disassembly tool, a hex key and a wooden dowel rod on the bench, and put everything else away. Rugged rules out a vise, pliers and any tool not named in this manual outright — the tube is thin-walled and the front cap and baffle faces are indexing surfaces, so a jaw mark is not cosmetic damage, it is a fit problem. If the can will not come apart with the sanctioned tools, the answer is solvent and time, not more grip.
steps.prose: A leaded-up rimfire can is the exact situation that tempts a vise. That is why the caution sits at the head of the teardown.
steps.quote: CAUTION! Do NOT use a vise, pliers, or tools other than outlined in this manual on your suppressor.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Oculus Disassembly, p.1
steps.warn: A vise or pliers on an Oculus22 is prohibited outright.

steps.title: Unscrew the whole can off the host
steps.action: With the firearm confirmed clear, unscrew the Oculus22 from the muzzle and set the gun aside. This is step one of the teardown, not a preliminary — every later operation happens with the can free on the bench. If it is hot from shooting, let it cool first; a hot can gripped hard is how people end up reaching for pliers.
steps.prose: Put the host down clear and open where you can see it. It stays that way for the rest of the job.
steps.quote: After removing the magazine of your firearm and checking the chamber of the firearm to confirm that it is in a safe condition and completely unloaded, remove the Oculus22 from the host firearm.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Oculus22 Disassembly, step 1, p.1

steps.title: ADAPT Module off the main body
steps.action: Hold the main suppressor body and rotate the ADAPT Module counter-clockwise until the two separate. Turn the module against a held body rather than the reverse, so the torque goes into the joint you want to open instead of into the baffle stack inside. You now have two tubes, each still full of baffles.
steps.prose: This is the same joint you use in the field to run the Oculus22 in its short configuration.
steps.quote: Remove the ADAPT Module from the main suppressor body by unscrewing it counter-clockwise.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Oculus22 Disassembly, step 2, p.1

steps.title: Push the main stack out from the mount end
steps.action: Look in through the mount at the rear of the main body and push the baffle cone forward with a finger or a wooden dowel rod until the stack walks out the front. The stack always leaves forwards — the way the bullet went — because the baffles taper that way. Wood is specified for the dowel deliberately: a steel rod on a baffle cone dents the one face that has to index square, and on a rimfire can that face is already the dirtiest part.
steps.prose: On a leaded stack this can take steady pressure rather than force. Steady pressure is the whole technique.
steps.quote: Remove the baffle stack from the main suppressor body by pushing forward on the baffle cone from inside the mount with your finger or a wooden dowel rod.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Oculus22 Disassembly, step 3, p.1

steps.title: Front cap off the module with the provided tool
steps.action: Fit the disassembly tool that came with the can into the front cap and turn counter-clockwise. That tool is the only thing that goes on this cap — it is why it was in the box, and it is what the no-vise-no-pliers caution is protecting. If it is carboned tight, wet the joint and wait rather than reaching for something with more grip.
steps.prose: This is a different tool from the Obsidian family, where the piston doubles as the cap wrench. Do not borrow that habit here.
steps.quote: Remove the front cap from the ADAPT Module using the provided disassembly tool.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Oculus22 Disassembly, step 4, p.1

steps.title: The module stack pushes out toward the front cap end
steps.action: The ADAPT Module's stack comes out in the opposite direction to the main body's: push on the baffle cone from the externally threaded end and drive it toward the front cap end. Get this backwards and you are pushing baffle cones against their own taper, which jams the stack tighter. Finger or wooden dowel again — nothing steel.
steps.prose: Two stacks, two directions. It is worth reading the direction off the part rather than off memory.
steps.quote: Remove the baffle stack from the ADAPT Module by pushing forward on the baffle cone from the externally threaded end towards the front cap end with your finger or a wooden dowel rod.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Oculus22 Disassembly, step 5, p.1

steps.title: Break the baffles apart one at a time — hex key, gently
steps.action: Separate the baffles one by one, and when a pair is stuck, put the long end of a hex key into a baffle port and pry gently against the inside of the baffle. Rugged capitalises GENTLY, and on a rimfire can that is the operative word: lead and wax glue the tapers together, so the temptation is to lever hard against a thin cone. Work the joint, re-wet it and try again rather than winning it in one go.
steps.prose: Lay the baffles out left to right in the order they came off, keeping the main body's five separate from the module's five.
steps.quote: Break the baffles apart one at a time. If the baffles are stuck together, a hex key can be used as a tool to aid in disassembly. Insert the long end of the key into the baffle port and GENTLY pry against the inside of the baffle to release it.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Oculus22 Disassembly, step 6, p.1

steps.title: Oculus22 thread check interval — between magazines, not at a round count
steps.action: Rugged sets the Oculus22's re-check interval by magazine, not by round count: unload the firearm, then confirm the can is still tight on the barrel, and do that between magazines. Thread-mounted suppressors back off under firing, and a direct-thread rimfire can with no locking collar has nothing but thread friction holding it. Note that this is the Oculus22's own interval and it is shorter than the 30-round figure Rugged prints for its centrefire pistol cans — do not carry a number across from another model.
steps.prose: A can that has walked partway off its threads is no longer concentric with the bore, and that is how a baffle strike starts.
steps.quote: WARNING! Since thread mounted suppressors may unscrew during firing, it is extremely important that the operator ensures the suppressor remains securely threaded to the barrel. The threading of the suppressor to the host firearm should be checked in between magazines AFTER first ensuring that the firearm is unloaded.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Mounting System, p.1
steps.warn: Check the thread between magazines, after confirming the firearm is unloaded.

steps.title: Never clean the Oculus22 on the gun
steps.action: Solvent, brushes and tanks only ever meet a can that is off the host and on the bench. Rugged states it as a death-risk warning, because cleaning means gripping and twisting a tube that would otherwise still be threaded to a muzzle with a chamber behind it. Confirm the host is clear, remove the suppressor, then clean.
steps.prose: It also protects the gun: 12-gauge bore brushes and brass wire on a rifle's muzzle crown is not a trade you want to make.
steps.quote: Never attempt to clean a suppressor while it is attached to a host weapon.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Service/Maintenance, p.2

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You should be looking at the main tube, the ADAPT Module, the front cap and two separate stacks of five baffles each. The main stack is one blast baffle, three standard and one short; the module carries four standard and one short. Keep the two apart — the counts are close enough that mixing them up is easy and the result is a can assembled wrong. Deep Clean covers the lead removal routine, the indexing that keeps your point of impact repeatable, and the port timing on rebuild.
steps.prose: Rimfire fouling sets hard. If you are not cleaning today, at least get the parts apart and dry rather than leaving a stack to seize.
steps.quote: The main baffle stack consists of 5 baffles —1 blast baffle, 3 standard baffles and 1 short baffle.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Main Baffle Stack Assembly, p.1

deepSteps.title: Ultrasonic the disassembled baffles — 50/50 Purple Power and water
deepSteps.action: Put the separated baffles into an ultrasonic tank charged with a 50/50 mix of Purple Power and water and run it for about an hour, then pull them out and let them dry. Rugged expects carbon to survive the cycle and says so; that residue is cosmetic. On a rimfire can the tank is doing most of the work that a brush would otherwise have to do to hard lead.
deepSteps.prose: They must go in disassembled. A stack cleaned as a column keeps the fouling exactly where it does harm — between the tapers.
deepSteps.quote: Rugged Suppressors recommends cleaning of the disassembled baffles with an ultrasonic cleaner using a 50/50 mixture of Purple Power® and water. Allow the baffles to be cleaned for approximately 1 hour, remove the parts and allow to dry.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Oculus Cleaning, p.2

deepSteps.title: The tube gets solvent, a 12 gauge bore brush and brass wire
deepSteps.action: The inside of the suppressor tube is cleaned with ordinary gun solvent and ordinary technique; Rugged names a 12 gauge bore brush and a brass wire brush as the tools for scrubbing carbon out of it. A 12 gauge brush in a .22 can sounds oversized and is exactly the point — the tube bore is far larger than the projectile, and a bore-sized brush would touch nothing.
deepSteps.prose: Brass, not steel. Brass is softer than the tube and will not score the bore it is cleaning.
deepSteps.quote: The inside of the suppressor tube can be cleaned using normal gun solvent and cleaning techniques. We recommend using a 12 gauge bore brush and a brass wire brush to remove any carbon as necessary.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Oculus Cleaning, p.2

deepSteps.title: Ventilation and hands — rimfire cleaning is a lead exposure
deepSteps.action: Do this work where there is real air movement and wash your hands thoroughly afterwards. Rugged names the hazard plainly: cleaning suppressors and shooting in poorly ventilated spaces exposes you to lead and to substances known to cause birth defects and reproductive harm. An Oculus22 is the worst offender in a collection for this, because unjacketed .22 deposits raw lead directly onto the baffles you are about to scrub.
deepSteps.prose: Gloves during the scrub, and do not eat or drink at the same bench.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING! Discharging firearms in poorly ventilated areas or cleaning suppressors may result in exposure to lead and other substances known to cause birth defects, reproductive harm, and other serious physical injury. Have adequate ventilation at all times. Wash hands throughly after exposure.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Service/Maintenance, p.2
deepSteps.warn: Ventilate, wear gloves, wash hands after.

deepSteps.title: Build the main stack on the bench, short baffle cone-up
deepSteps.action: Assemble the five-baffle main stack on a flat, level surface starting with the short baffle, cone facing up, then index each following baffle onto it through the machined tabs. Building it as a free-standing column is what lets you see whether the tabs actually engaged — a stack built inside the tube cannot be inspected at all. Blast baffle last, and Rugged identifies it for you with a #1 engraved on its body.
deepSteps.prose: Squeeze the finished column and look for daylight between baffles; a rubber mallet seats a gap, force does not.
deepSteps.quote: Start by placing the short baffle on a flat, level surface with the cone facing up.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Main Baffle Stack Assembly, step 1, p.1

deepSteps.title: Index the stack to the same flat every time — the serial number is the mark
deepSteps.action: When the assembled stack drops into the main body, the blast baffle's indexing tabs have to engage the indexing flats machined inside the tube; you get an audible click when it is home. Rugged engraves the Oculus22's serial number over one indexing tab specifically so you can put the stack back at the same clock position after every clean. Line that engraved tab up with the same flat each time and your point of impact shift from disassembly stays minimal.
deepSteps.prose: This is the single habit that separates a rimfire can that shoots the same after cleaning from one that does not.
deepSteps.quote: The Oculus22™ serial number is engraved over an indexing tab to aid in repeatable alignment of the baffle stack.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Main Baffle Stack Assembly, step 7, p.1

deepSteps.title: Module stack in, then time the ports about 1/8 turn counterclockwise
deepSteps.action: Thread the empty module onto the body, build its five-baffle stack the same way — short baffle cone-up, then the standard baffles — and drop it into the tube. As the end cap seats it will rotate the stack slightly, so Rugged tells you to pre-align the module ports roughly an eighth of a turn counterclockwise of the body's ports, which lands them correct once everything is tight. Then screw the front cap on with the provided tool; tightening seats the cap into the last baffle.
deepSteps.prose: Check the gap between the main body and the module against Figure A before you trust it — an incorrect gap means the baffles are not seated to the indexing tab.
deepSteps.quote: Insert the assembled ADAPT Module baffle stack into the tube. As the end cap seats into the baffle stack, and may cause the stack to rotate slightly, it may be necessary to align the ADAPT Module ports approximately 1/8 of a turn to counterclockwise of the suppressor body baffle stack ports to ensure correct alignment when fully assembled.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — ADAPT Module Assembly, step 6, p.1

deepSteps.title: Check the body-to-module gap against Figure A
deepSteps.action: With the module threaded onto the body, look at the seam between the two and compare it against Figure A in the manual. A correct gap means the baffles are seated onto their indexing tab; too large a gap means they are not, and the stack inside is sitting on something it should not be. This is a check you can make from the outside without opening the can again, which is exactly why it exists.
deepSteps.prose: Correct spacing between main body and module means the baffles are correctly seated. Wrong spacing is not a tolerance, it is a fault.
deepSteps.quote: Check to see the gap between the main body of the suppressor and the ADAPT module is correct by referring to “Figure A“ on the reverse side.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — ADAPT Module Assembly, step 1, p.1

deepSteps.title: Cool it before you change configuration
deepSteps.action: Going between the short and long configurations means unscrewing the ADAPT Module, and Rugged requires the body to be back at ambient temperature before you do that. Threads that are at very different temperatures do not run cleanly against each other, and a hot module backed off a hot body is how they gall. On the range this is the rule most often broken, because the whole point of a modular can is changing it between strings.
deepSteps.prose: Wait it out. The alternative is a module that will not come off at all.
deepSteps.quote: When changing between the short and long configurations; make sure the suppressor body has cooled to ambient temperatures before attaching/detaching the ADAPT™ Module.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OCULUS22 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — ADAPT Module Assembly, p.1
deepSteps.warn: Ambient temperature before attaching or detaching the module.

cleaning.name: BAFFLES (disassembled)
tasks: Separate every baffle before cleaning — never clean the stack as a column
Ultrasonic in a 50/50 mix of Purple Power and water, about one hour, then dry
Residual carbon after the cycle is acceptable and does not have to be removed
Hex key GENTLY in a baffle port to break a stuck pair; never a vise or pliers

cleaning.name: SUPPRESSOR TUBE & ADAPT MODULE
tasks: Normal gun solvent and normal cleaning technique inside the tube
A 12 gauge bore brush and a brass wire brush for carbon — brass, never steel
Clear the internal threads and the front cap's tool interface
Check the body-to-module gap against Figure A once reassembled

cleaning.name: MOUNT & HOST THREADS
tasks: The can seats against a 90-degree barrel shoulder; if it tightens before it seats or stays loose after, stop and contact Rugged
Re-check the thread between magazines while shooting, after confirming the firearm is unloaded
Keep the barrel shoulder and mount face free of lead and carbon so the can seats square

cleaning.name: SAFETY DURING CLEANING
tasks: Suppressor off the host firearm before any cleaning begins
Adequate ventilation at all times — this is a lead exposure
Wash hands thoroughly after handling rimfire fouling

reassembly: Build the main stack on a flat level surface: short baffle cone-up, three standard baffles, blast baffle #1 last.
Check for spacing between baffles and seat any gap with a rubber mallet.
Insert the main stack into the main suppressor body with the #1 blast baffle cone facing down.
Align the blast baffle's indexing tabs with the indexing flats inside the body until it clicks; use the serial-number-engraved tab as your repeatable reference.
Thread the empty ADAPT Module onto the main body and check the body-to-module gap against Figure A.
Build the module's five-baffle stack — short baffle cone-up, then four standard baffles.
Insert the module stack pre-aligned about 1/8 of a turn counterclockwise of the body stack's ports.
Screw the front cap on with the provided tool; tightening seats the cap into the last baffle.
fncheck: Look through the bore against a light and confirm it is clear with no baffle edge intruding. Confirm the body-to-module gap matches Figure A — a wide gap means the baffles are not seated to their indexing tab. Confirm the front cap is tight with the provided tool and nothing rattles. The Oculus22 seats against a 90-degree barrel shoulder; if it goes tight before it seats, or stays loose after it seats, stop and contact Rugged. While shooting, re-check the thread between magazines, after first confirming the firearm is unloaded.
